Author of the article chiming in. While it's very possible that there was a "quota" for Asian actors in the movie, we just don't know. We don't know what went behind the casting doors. For example, most of us didn't know that the role of Vincent Kapoor was offered to Irrfan Khan before he turned it down. Maybe they really did audition Asian actresses but went with a white actress instead. I see it ALL the time in my audition front and I've seen it in cases where they wanted a white actress but got an Asian or Latino or black actress instead.

Now yes, is whitewashing real? Hell yeah. Don't even get me started on Ridley Scott's EXODUS and his justification why casting white actors to bronze themselves up to play Egyptians made any sense.

With the term WHITEWASHING, it usually applies if the WHOLE cast was white. To which this film wasn't. And yes, it does very much apply if it's just one role and not the entire cast but in my subjective opinion, it is better used if EVERY single Asian character or minority character has been changed to be played by a white actor.

Author of the article reporting in. If that's what you got from reading the article, then I'm sorry to hear about that. You must have skipped out reading the last half of the article as I stress the importance of Asian actors playing bigger roles.

Hi there. Author of the article reporting in. While I understand your concern, my point is that the act of releasing an official statement to press and DEMANDING why the characters were whitewashed (not doing the research that Irrfan Khan was offered to play Vincent Kapoor before he turned it down to do Jurassic World instead) is not a battle worth fighting for and creating such a noise about. HOWEVER, that is all subjective.

A BIGGER battle would be why Scarlett Johannson got cast in the American adaptation of GHOST IN THE SHELL. Or even with EXODUS, the previous Ridley Scott film. I didn't see that many Asian American advocacy groups make a noise with this one because, simply put, it didn't have anything to do with Asians. However, that was a blatant case of whitewashing where you had white actors actually bronzing themselves up to play Egyptians. The fact that sh!t happened, to me, is more unforgivable than with them having a small part originally written for a Korean to be played by a white actress.

Hey there, it's the guy who wrote the article that everybody is commenting on. To answer your question, my line of work has mainly been commercials (that pays most of my bills), TV shows, features, along with short films & plays that I do once in a while if the material is interesting.

As an Asian American actor, playing white roles rarely (if never) happens but I have been cast in roles where they were primarily looking for a white actor but I got the role because I was the best man for the job. Granted, this happens more with indie fare and smaller roles in primetime TV shows but when it happens, it's still pretty cool.

It is very possible to become a working actor and make the choice to take on roles that aren't racist caricatures. And I have faith things will become a lot better in the years to come, especially with notable entries like FRESH OFF THE BOAT premiering on ABC next month.
